steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: GCSE Latin prose set texts are prescribed by each exam board and change every two years. You must check which texts are current for your year of examination. | Key Fact: Common prose authors include Caesar (De Bello Gallico), Cicero (speeches and letters), Tacitus (Annales), Pliny the Younger (Letters), and Livy (Ab Urbe Condita). | Key Fact: Caesar's De Bello Gallico describes his conquest of Gaul (58-50 BC): key themes include Roman imperialism, leadership, and the clash between Roman and barbarian cultures. | Key Fact: Cicero's works include political speeches (In Catilinam against Catiline) and personal letters that reveal late Republican politics and daily life.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on GCSE Latin Exam Tips — Prose Set Texts, and one past-paper question.
